read the number at eye level

order: money in take away money out is the profit

little.twist: A customer asks for something you don't sell, and nothing glows to help.
little.can_now: ask customers what they would like, set a fair price, count coins and change, and keep some money to make more

steps.say: Your very own stand! You sell bread and cakes made from the farm's wheat. These are pretend coins.
Every stand needs a sign. Which sign tells people what you sell?

choices.why: A blank sign tells nobody what you sell.
You don't sell toys! A sign should tell the truth.

steps.done: Now everyone knows what you sell.

steps.say: Put your bread and your cake out on the stand.
steps.done: Ready for customers.

steps.say: {one_mood} What do you say?

choices.why: Ask first! Then you know what they want.
A hello and a question make customers feel welcome.

steps.done: Asking first is how you know what people want.

steps.say: "Do you have pies?" You only sell bread and cakes. What do you say?

choices.text: Sorry, no pies. Would you like bread or a cake?

choices.why: Be honest about what you sell. Then offer what you have.
Say sorry kindly, and offer what you do have.

steps.done: Honest and kind: "No pies, but I have bread and cakes!"

steps.say: {one_name} says: "{one_wish}" What will you give?

choices.why: Listen again: {one_name} asked for {one_good_one}.

steps.done: That's just what {one_name} wanted.

steps.say: Take {one_good_one} from your stand.
steps.done: Here you are!

steps.say: Take {one_good_one} from your stand.
steps.done: Here you are!

steps.say: It cost you {cost} coin to make. What is a fair price?

choices.text: {price} coins: the cost and a little more

choices.why: So much that nobody could pay! A fair price is the cost and a little more.
Then you have no money to buy flour and make more.

steps.done: A fair price: good for {one_name}, and good for you.

steps.say: {one_name} pays {price} coins. Put them in your cash box, coin by coin.
steps.done: {price} coins in the cash box.

steps.say: Give it to {one_name}, and say thank you!
steps.done: "Thank you!" {one_name} gives your stand 5 stars.

steps.say: Mo comes for bread. Bread is 2 coins. He gives you {two_paid} coins.
Give Mo {two_change} coins change, coin by coin.
steps.done: 2 and {two_change} make {two_paid}. The right change!

steps.say: Give Mo his bread.
steps.done: Mo says: "Fresh bread and a big smile!"

steps.say: Keep {flour_out} coins in the FLOUR jar, to buy flour for tomorrow.
steps.done: Money in, some money out for flour: that's how a stand keeps going.

steps.say: You took {money_in} coins and kept {flour_out} for flour. How many coins are left for you?

choices.why: Take away the flour money first.
Count again: {money_in} take away {flour_out}.

steps.done: {left} coins: your profit!

steps.say: Wonderful! You asked what people wanted, gave the right things, gave change, and kept money for flour.

check.say: A customer comes to your stand. What do you say first?
A cake cost 1 coin to make. A fair price?
Why keep some coins after you sell?

choices.text: To buy flour and make more

lines: A fair price: the cost and a little more.
Give the right change, and say thank you.
Keep some money to make more.

sources.fact: Making something people want and selling it: spotting what others value (value for others).

middle.skill: My shop: customers, prices and reviews
middle.twist: Flour costs more this week, a second customer waits while you serve, and nothing glows to help.
middle.can_now: ask customers what they want, price for a profit, give change, fix a complaint kindly, pay a fair wage, read a ledger and win customers back with quality, never tricks

steps.say: Your own bakery! Bread, cakes and honey buns from the farm's wheat. Customers come while you are here. These are pretend coins.
Your shop needs a sign. Which one is clear and honest?

choices.text: FRESH BREAD, CAKES AND HONEY BUNS
THE BEST BAKERY IN THE WHOLE WORLD!
choices.why: Can you show that's true? A sign should be clear and honest.
It doesn't say what you sell.

steps.done: Clear and honest: customers know what you sell.

steps.say: A loaf costs you 2 coins to make: 1 for flour, 1 for butter and salt. Which price is fair?

choices.text: 3 coins: the cost and a little profit

choices.why: Too high: customers go somewhere else, and nobody buys.
Too low: you make nothing, and there is no money left for more flour.

steps.done: Price = what it costs + a little profit. Cakes are 4 and honey buns 2, the same way.

steps.say: Flour costs more this week: a loaf now costs you 3 coins to make. Which price is fair?

choices.text: 4 coins: the cost and a little profit

choices.why: Much more than the cost went up: customers notice and go elsewhere.
That's only what it costs now: nothing for your work or more flour.

steps.done: When a cost goes up, a fair price goes up a little. Tell customers why.

steps.say: {one_mood} What do you say first?

choices.why: Ask first: people buy what they want, not what you push.
A friendly hello and a question help, most of all with a shy customer.

steps.done: Ask what people want: that's how a shop knows what to make.

steps.say: {one_name}: "{one_wish}" What will you get?

choices.why: Listen again: {one_name} asked for {one_good_one}.
Listen again: {one_name} asked for {one_good_one}.

steps.done: Just what {one_name} wanted.

steps.say: Take {one_what} from the shelf.
steps.done: Here you are.

steps.say: Take {one_what} from the shelf.
steps.done: Here you are.

steps.say: While you serve {one_name}, {two_name} comes in and waits. What do you say?

choices.text: Hello! I'll be with you in a moment.

choices.why: A quick hello tells waiting customers you've seen them.
Rude words send customers away for good.

steps.done: A kind word while they wait: customers feel seen.

steps.say: {one_name} pays with a 10 coin for {one_total}. Give {one_change} coins change, coin by coin.
steps.done: {one_total} and {one_change} make 10.

steps.say: Give it to {one_name}, and say thank you.
steps.done: {one_name} leaves a review on your board: 5 stars!

steps.say: {two_name} comes in, but can't decide. What could you ask?

choices.why: Help people find what they need, not the dearest thing.
Customers wait kindly here: there's no rush.

steps.done: "It's for my friends. I have {two_budget} coins."

steps.say: Honey buns are 2 coins each. How many can {two_name} buy with {two_budget} coins?

choices.why: Each bun is 2 coins: share {two_budget} into twos.
Count in twos up to {two_budget}.

steps.done: {two_count} honey buns, one for each friend.

steps.say: {two_name} pays {two_budget} coins. Put them in the till, coin by coin.
steps.done: In the till. {two_name} takes the honey buns home.

steps.say: Time to bake more! Weigh {flour_g} grams of flour on the scales.
steps.done: {flour_g} grams. That flour cost {flour_cost} coins: money out.

steps.label: Baking: 30 minutes
steps.say: Into the oven! Bobo, your helper, takes the hot tray out with oven gloves.
steps.done: Fresh bread!

steps.say: Mo comes back, a little cross: "{gripe}" What do you do first?

choices.text: "It was fine when it left here!"
choices.why: That's arguing. Listen first, then say sorry.
Stay and listen: a complaint is a chance to fix things.

steps.done: "{gripe_back}" Mo nods: you listened.

steps.say: Say sorry, and fix it: give Mo a fresh loaf.
steps.done: "Thank you for listening!" Mo smiles again.

steps.say: Bobo helped all afternoon. Pay him a fair wage: {wage} coins.
steps.done: Thank you, Bobo! Fair pay for fair work.

steps.say: Your ledger: money in {money_in}, money out {money_out} (flour {flour_cost}, Bobo's wage {wage}). What is your profit?

choices.why: Money out is taken away, not added.
Don't forget the money that went out.

steps.done: {profit} coins profit: money in take away money out.

steps.say: The ledger's bars show this week's profit, day by day. Which day made the most?

choices.why: Look for the tallest bar.
Look for the tallest bar.

steps.done: {best_day}! The bars show which days are busy.

steps.say: Read your review board: what do your customers say?
steps.done: Honest reviews tell you what to keep, and what to make better.

steps.say: Across the square, Pip-pop opens a bakery, and some customers go there. How do you win them back?

choices.text: Write pretend 5-star reviews of your shop
choices.why: Fake reviews are lies: customers stop trusting you, and real shops are not allowed to use them.
Saying untrue things about someone is unfair and unkind. Win with quality, never with tricks.

steps.done: Customers come back for good bread and a kind welcome.

steps.say: A real shopkeeper! You asked, priced fairly, gave change, fixed a complaint, paid a fair wage and read your ledger. Honest wins.

check.say: A loaf costs 2 coins to make. Which price makes a profit?
Money in 12, money out 5. What is the profit?
A new shop opens nearby. How do you keep your customers?

name_it.title: Running a shop
lines: Price = what it costs + a little profit.
A complaint: listen, say sorry, fix it.
The ledger: money in, money out, profit.
Win customers with quality and service, never tricks.
name_it.source: EntreComp (2016), the OECD/INFE framework (2015) and the UK's Competition and Markets Authority on fake reviews

middle.try_real: Help a grown-up compare two prices in a shop: which is the better buy, and why?

sources.fact: Turning ideas into value for others; finding out what customers need; working with others (a helper).
sources.source: EntreComp, the EU's Entrepreneurship Competence Framework (2016)

sources.fact: Prices, costs and profit; comparing prices; keeping records of money in and out.
sources.source: OECD/INFE Core Competencies Framework on Financial Literacy for Youth (2015)

sources.fact: Fake reviews, positive or negative, are banned by law in the UK (from 6 April 2025).
sources.source: Competition and Markets Authority, Fake reviews guidance (CMA208, 2025)

sources.fact: A complaint: listen, say it back, say sorry, fix it, thank them (Talk & Deal's way).

big.skill: Harder days: costs, rain, orders and a rival
big.twist: The big order's honey comes a day late: tell Mr Okafor early. And nothing glows to help.
big.can_now: change a price fairly when costs rise, bake for the customers expected, take and keep a big order, work out and pay a fair wage, read a loss in the ledger, keep a fair price in a price war, answer an unfair review kindly and save to grow

steps.say: Your bakery's harder days: dearer flour, a rainy day, a big order, a fair wage and a rival. These are pretend coins.
A loaf cost you {old_cost} coins to make. Now its flour costs {flour_up} coin more. What does a loaf cost you now?

choices.why: Add the dearer flour to the cost.
Only the flour went up, by {flour_up}.

steps.done: {new_cost} coins to make a loaf now.

steps.say: What is your new fair price for a loaf?

choices.text: {new_price} coins: the new cost and your profit

choices.why: That is no more than a loaf costs you now: no profit for your work, or for next week's flour.
That's far more than the cost went up: customers notice and go elsewhere.

steps.done: When costs rise, a fair price rises a little. Tell customers why: honesty keeps their trust.

steps.say: Rain today: about half the usual customers. You usually bake {normal_loaves} loaves. How many today?

choices.why: Bread nobody buys is money wasted: flour, butter and work.
Some customers still come in the rain!

steps.done: Bake for the customers you expect: less waste, more profit.

steps.say: Mr Okafor orders {order_n} honey buns for the library's party on Saturday, at 2 coins each. What is the total?

choices.why: {order_n} buns at 2 coins each: multiply, don't add.
Each bun is 2 coins, not 1.

steps.done: {order_total} coins. "See you on Saturday!"

steps.say: Weigh {honey_g} grams of honey for the buns. Slowly near the end!
steps.done: {honey_g} grams. The honey cost {honey_cost} coins: money out.

steps.say: Oh no: the honey for the rest of the buns comes a day late. Saturday is the party. What do you do?

choices.text: Tell Mr Okafor early, and agree a new plan

choices.why: Bad news told early can be fixed together. Silence breaks trust.

choices.text: Use no honey and don't tell him
choices.why: That isn't what he ordered. Be honest, then fix it together.

steps.done: "Thank you for telling me early. Half on Saturday, half on Sunday is fine!"

steps.label: Saturday
steps.say: The buns are baked, and Saturday comes.
steps.done: Mr Okafor is here for his order.

steps.say: Hand Mr Okafor his order.
steps.done: "Just as you promised!" A promise kept builds trust.

steps.say: Hand Mr Okafor his order.
steps.done: "Just as we agreed!" Telling him early kept his trust.

steps.say: {one_mood} {one_name} buys 2 loaves at {new_price} and pays with a 20 note. Give {one_change} coins change.
steps.done: {one_total} and {one_change} make 20.

steps.say: Bobo worked {hours} hours. A fair wage is {rate} coins an hour. What do you owe him?

choices.why: {hours} hours at {rate} coins an hour: multiply.
That's one hour. Bobo worked {hours}.

steps.done: {wage} coins for {hours} hours.

steps.say: Pay Bobo his {wage} coins.
steps.done: Paid in full and on time: good helpers stay with fair bosses.

steps.say: Your ledger's week: one bar dips under the line, a loss. Which day, and why?

choices.text: {loss_day}: rain, and too much bread baked

choices.why: That's the tallest bar: the most profit.
Only one bar is under the line.

steps.done: A loss happens. The ledger shows why, so you can plan better next time.

steps.say: Pip-pop sells bread at 1 coin, less than it costs her to make. Do you go lower too?

choices.text: No: keep a fair price, and show your quality

choices.why: Below the cost every loaf loses money, and soon there is none left for flour.
That's untrue and unkind. Win with quality, never with tricks.

steps.done: Selling below the cost can't last. Quality and kindness can.

steps.say: A review says "Not a nice bakery" from someone who never came in. What do you do?

choices.text: Reply kindly and honestly, and invite them in

choices.why: Fake reviews are lies, and real shops are not allowed to use them.
Rude words make it worse, and everyone can read them.

steps.done: A kind, honest reply shows everyone what your shop is really like.

steps.say: This month's profit is {month_profit}. A bigger oven costs {oven}. You put {save_part} aside each month. How many months?

choices.why: Count how many lots of {save_part} make {oven}.
{save_part} a month is not {oven} yet.

steps.done: {months} months of saving, and the bakery can grow.

steps.say: Your shop is doing well. The school's fair asks the village for help. What would you like to do?

choices.reply: Kind: the village remembers shops that give back.
Sharing what you know helps others start.

choices.text: Save a little first, then give
choices.reply: A good plan: look after the shop, and give too.

steps.say: You handled dearer flour, rain, a big order, a fair wage, a rival and an unfair review, all honestly. For real money, talk to a grown-up you trust.

check.say: The flour gets dearer. A fair price...

choices.text: goes up a little, and you say why

check.say: Rain halves your customers. You bake...
A rival sells below what it costs. You...

choices.text: keep a fair price and good quality

check.say: A fair wage for 3 hours at 3 coins an hour?

name_it.title: A business on harder days
lines: When costs rise, a fair price rises a little: say why.
Make what customers will buy: less waste.
A promise is a deal: bad news, tell it early.
Pay a fair wage for the time worked.
Never sell below the cost, and never use tricks.
name_it.source: EntreComp (2016), the EU and OECD financial competence framework (2023) and the Competition and Markets Authority (2025)
